newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call rate unchanged despite higher turnover.
newsitem.headline: Manila call rate unchanged despite higher turnover.

text.p: The Philippine call loan rate was stuck at 16.03125 percent despite a higher turnover of 11.503 billion pesos on Friday, traders said.
Friday sessions are usually the dullest since most banks have already squared their reserves positions for the week.
"It seems that some banks went to the market to cover their reserve deficiencies after paying for their 10-year T-bond purchase," one trader said.
The government auctioned 3.5 billion pesos worth of 10-year T-bonds on Wednesday, with settlement date on Thursday.
However, the market was able to absorb the higher demand since other banks were still awash with cash, he said.
He said some banks have been attracting short-term deposits to beef up their cash positions for month-end window-dressing.
Done rates ranged from 16.0 to 16.4375 percent.
The secondary Treasury bill market was likewise listless with buyers outnumbering sellers of bills.
"Some banks were aggressively looking for short-term instruments. But there were no sellers to feed their appetite," one trader said.
"Other than that, the market is very quiet," he added.
Bids for the 91-day bills were at 10.65 to 10.85 percent, lower than the average T-bill rate awarded last Tuesday.
